atoms.b: Relative pronouns connect ((++relative adjectival)) clauses to ((++independent_clauses adverbs)).
Usually, they offer ((++additional less)) information about something ((++already not_yet)) mentioned in a sentence.

For example:
Do you remember the film ((++that when)) I was telling you about?

Or:
Her uncle, ((++who why)) is a professional pastry chef, prepared an incredible chocolate cake for her birthday.

atoms.a: What do the relative pronouns who and whom usually refer to?
atoms.b: Who and whom usually refer to ((++people --objects)).
Which and that usually refer to ((++animals_and_things --family_and_friends)).

instruction.text: Complete the sentences by choosing the correct relative pronoun.

atoms.a: We were going to go with people _____ had lots of experience with water-rafting.
atoms.sound: We were going to go with people who had lots of experience with water-rafting

atoms.a: I think the party, _____ I had planned, will have to be cancelled.
atoms.sound: I think the party, which I had planned, will have to be cancelled.

atoms.a: She knows of a place _____ you can get high-quality second-hand clothing.
atoms.sound: She knows of a place where you can get high quality second-hand clothing.

atoms.a: He wasn’t too sure _____ dirty socks they were, but he wore them anyway.
atoms.sound: He wasn’t too sure whose dirty socks they were, but he wore them anyway

atoms.a: Do you know _____ it is important to floss your teeth?
atoms.sound: Do you know why it is important to floss your teeth?
